items.title: What I Think of The Results of the U.S. Midterm Elections
items.position: The election changes who handles the problems (debt, wealth/values gap, geopolitics, climate, technology), not the problems; he expects brutal fights over spending and taxes around the Dec 11 funding expiry, a March 2027 debt-limit hit and a fall-2027 point where Treasury runs out of options, pushing short-term Treasury yields up and raising doubts about Treasuries as the world's safe collateral. The only workable path is moderates of both parties cooperating on hard fiscal changes, which he calls unlikely; a wounded lame-duck presidency means US retrenchment abroad.

items.name: Brad Setser
items.title: Three Questions About China's Hidden Foreign Exchange Assets
items.position: The PBOC says it has no hidden reserves, but Setser argues it has hidden foreign-currency assets: FX settlement purchases of $500-600bn over the last 12 months against a ~$50bn rise in the PBOC balance sheet, a cumulative unexplained gap near $1 trillion, missing reinvested interest income (~$100bn/yr on ~$3tn), and entrusted loans/swaps to policy banks that never flow back. The monthly pattern looks like backdoor intervention holding a tight band around a crawling peg; the weak RMB underpins China's export outperformance since 2023, continuing in 2026.
